title: Docket Clerk's Note on the First-Setting Clock — Unemployment Insurance Appeals
content:
The *first-setting clock* is the day from which an appeal's first hearing date is counted, in calendar days, when the first hearing is set under Unemployment Insurance Appeals. The day the clock starts turns on two facts on the appeal record: whether a late-filing reason is recorded, and the channel the appeal came in by.

**Rule.** The first-setting clock starts today, the day the appeal is docketed, for an appeal filed after its deadline with a good-cause reason stated; it starts on the presumed receipt date, the presumed mail receipt days after the postmark date, for an appeal filed with no late-filing reason by mail; and it starts on the appeal's filing date for an appeal filed with no late-filing reason online or by fax. The presumed mail receipt days are **3** calendar days.

## Clock start by record

| Late-filing reason on the appeal record | Filing channel | First-setting clock starts on |
|---|---|---|
| a good-cause reason is stated (any reason other than none) | any | today, the day the appeal is docketed |
| none | mail | the presumed receipt date: 3 calendar days after the postmark date |
| none | online portal or fax | the appeal's filing date (the online submission or fax date) |

The late-filing reason decides first: once a good-cause reason is recorded, the channel no longer matters. For an appeal with no late-filing reason, the channel decides between the presumed receipt date and the filing date. For a mailed appeal the filing date is the postmark date, so the presumed receipt date is the postmark date moved 3 calendar days later.

## Worked dates (hypothetical; the appeal is docketed on Wednesday 15 April 2026)

| Appeal | Late-filing reason | Channel | Filing date | Clock starts |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | none | mail | postmark Monday 6 April | Thursday 9 April |
| B | none | online portal | Monday 6 April | Monday 6 April |
| C | none | fax | Friday 10 April | Friday 10 April |
| D | good cause stated (filed after the deadline) | mail | postmark Monday 6 April | Wednesday 15 April (today) |

Appeals A and B were filed on the same day; A's clock starts 3 days later because it came by mail. Appeal D came by mail as well, but the stated good-cause reason places its clock on the docketing day.
